In metal the positive ions of metals are surrounded by sea of mobile electrons and the force of attraction occur between metal ion and mobile electrons which is placed uniform in all directions. The metal ions are held together by strong force in crystal lattice. Due to this one layer of metal can slide over other when they are stretched and hammered. That is why metals are malleable and ductile.
68. Why is solid sodium chloride a non conductor of electricity?
Solid sodium chloride is an ionic compound and ions present in sodium chloride is strongly held together by an electrostatic force of attraction. They are strongly fixed in crystal lattice.
Hence, there are no mobile electrons or free electrons in solid state of sodium chloride. So, sodium chloride is non-conductor of electricity.
